acceptanceCriteria.text: One production Route 3 invocation can take an exact canonical Appliance plus desired release/generation intent from missing instance to active managed Runtime without a human logging into the guest.
The canonical first-boot control/authentication mechanism works through Lima without broad HOME key import and without changing the guest into a Lima-specific image.
The desired managed-package manifest/generation intent is materialized automatically from release input; no manual guest file injection is required on the golden path.
Production orchestration invokes the canonical guest bootstrap/reconcile boundary and verifies the exact desired/active generation identity.
A guest reporting only `bootstrapReady=true` cannot make Route 3 return success when `managedRuntimeReady` for the intended generation is false.
Final Route 3 success proves representative packaged Mottainai CLI and MCP behavior inside the active managed generation.
Repeated ensure on an unchanged healthy instance is a no-op and does not rebuild/re-activate the current generation unnecessarily.
A failed new generation preserves/returns to known-good state according to the canonical bootstrap rollback contract and Route 3 reports the failure truthfully.

Tests cover fresh bootstrap-only guest, already-managed current guest, wrong/stale generation, bootstrap failure, activation health failure/rollback, lost/restarted instance, and no-op convergence with hermetic provider/guest fixtures where possible.
Real Linux/KVM certification remains #261; this Issue exhausts repository-CI-provable Route 3 composition first.

issue.title: feat(runtime): make Route 3 converge the Lima Runtime to managed Mottainai readiness
